raw_response:
I am 70 years old and have farmed these flat fields of Quzhou County since I was a young man. My family has about 5 mu of good irrigated land, and I know every corner of it. At my age, I do not chase risky new crops—I stick to what has fed my family and paid the bills for decades.

This year, like every year, I will grow winter wheat and summer maize in rotation. That is what this soil and climate are made for, and the grain dealers come right to the village to buy. I will plant improved wheat seed in early October. Before sowing, I will hire a rotary tiller to prepare the ground—turning the stubble under and leveling the field so the water spreads evenly when I irrigate. For fertilizer, I will spread about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as a base, and then top-dress with urea at green-up and jointing. All told, that comes to about 18 kg of nitrogen, 11 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times: once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling, pumping from the village well. I will spray herbicide once after sowing, insecticide twice when the aphids show up, and fungicide once if I see yellow rust starting.

After I harvest the wheat around early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize—Denghai 605 or something similar from the seed shop. There is no time to waste between crops, so I will plant no-till right into the wheat stubble. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat here because the soil still holds some from the wheat season; I will put down about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, giving roughly 11 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice, at the big-flare and filling stages, and spray herbicide once and insecticide twice to control armyworms and corn borers.

I expect the wheat to yield about 500 kg per mu and the maize about 550 kg per mu. Some people plant cotton or vegetables, but I am too old for that kind of gamble. Wheat and maize are safe, the government gives a small subsidy for wheat, and I can sell the surplus or feed the corn to the few pigs my son raises.
